Ligand 1 is the 4-methyl cyclobutyl molecule at Phi 2.286; atom 15 is its cyclobutane CH bonded to the carbonyl at atom 13, so anchoring there keeps the four-membered cap. The 4-methyl is costing about 0.04 of activity against a halogen, so replacing it is close to free, and I am using this cell to put a methoxy on the cyclobutyl cap - the middle option on both axes. Cyclobutyl sits between cyclopropyl and oxetane on the SA-versus-QED trade, and methoxy sits between the halogens and the alkyls on lipophilicity while matching chlorine's mass. If the methoxy carries activity like a halogen, this should land close to my best without any single extreme choice, which is useful to know: it would mean the series tolerates a whole band of substituents rather than depending on one. Everything that carries activity is unchanged. Expected product: about 297 Da.
